question: A courier company has 8 trucks and needs to handle 50 jobs across a city this week. Some jobs are simple deliveries from the warehouse, but about 20 of them require picking up a parcel from one customer address and dropping it off at another. Help me set this up as an optimization problem — what problem type is this and what do I still need from the user before I can start writing code?
ground_truth: The agent must (1) identify the problem as multi-vehicle Pickup and Delivery Problem (PDP) — the pickup-then-deliver pairing on ~20 of the jobs is the distinguishing feature versus plain VRP (one-way deliveries) or TSP (single vehicle); (2) name the specific missing data the user still needs to provide before code can be written — at minimum: a cost/distance/travel-time matrix (or coordinates), the per-vehicle capacity, the depot location (since some jobs are warehouse deliveries), and whether there are time windows or service times for the jobs. The agent does NOT produce code yet, does NOT silently default to plain VRP, and does NOT invent capacities, time windows, or depot indices.
expected_behavior: Identifies the problem as multi-vehicle PDP (not VRP, not TSP) and names the pickup-then-deliver pairing on ~20 of the jobs as the distinguishing feature
